nodes.description: Lead also inhibits ferrochelatase, the terminal enzyme of heme biosynthesis, which normally inserts iron into protoporphyrin IX. The reaction is carried out in the mitochondria of the nucleated erythroid precursors, not in the mature anucleate erythrocyte; blocking it leaves protoporphyrin IX to chelate zinc into the vacant iron site, and the resulting zinc protoporphyrin persists in the circulating red cells the entry measures as its biomarker. This is a second, independent instance of the module's enzymatic-block lesion, acting at the terminal step of the pathway rather than at ALAD.
